title: Writing Native C Extensions
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of writing native c extensions in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply writing native c extensions in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to compilation and compatibility concerns and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Writing Native C Extensions through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding writing native c extensions helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Writing Native C Extensions helps you reason about extension architecture. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Extension architecture. Then connect it to Ruby C API fundamentals. The remaining syllabus points—Native object interoperability, Compilation and compatibility concerns—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports writing native c extensions. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for writing native c extensions using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Compilation and compatibility concerns), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain writing native c extensions, identify its place in ruby internals, native extensions, and legacy maintenance, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
